After two years of silence, Apple is reportedly developing a new iMac featuring the M6 chip and updated colour options, expected to launch "by the end of this year," according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman.

The iMac's update cycle has never been particularly frequent — it skipped both the M2 and M5 chip generations, and there is still no larger screen size option available. Instead, Apple has been steering high-end users toward pairing a Studio Display with a Mac Studio or Mac mini. However, the company is indeed preparing a new version equipped with the M6 chip.

Gurman noted that this update will include "some new colour options," but did not reveal any specific changes. Apple already made subtle adjustments to its colour palette during the 2024 M4 refresh, maintaining seven colour choices while using different shades. The new iMac is also expected to arrive before the end of the year:

This autumn could prove to be a significant season for the Mac lineup. The product range includes: a brand-new MacBook Pro model with a touchscreen and Tandem OLED display, an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip, new Mac Studio models with M5 Max and M5 Ultra (subject to availability), and an updated iMac featuring the M6 chip. There may also be a new Mac mini equipped with M6 and M5 Pro chips, though this product might arrive later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip built on the new 2nm process, but there are reportedly no M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra variants in the works — Apple is instead accelerating the rollout of the M7 generation.
